title: The board and its square names
outcomes: Names any square from its file and rank
Finds a named square on the board, from White's side or Black's
Reads a simple written move such as Nf3 or Bc4 and plays it

steps.text: A chessboard has 64 squares. The columns are called **files** and are named with the letters **a** to **h**, left to right as White sees the board. The rows are called **ranks** and are numbered **1** to **8**, starting at White's side. Every square has a name: its file letter, then its rank number. The white king starts on **e1**.

steps.caption: Watch the white pawn travel from e2 to e4. Every square keeps its name.

line.say: The pawn on e2 moves to e4.
Black's pawn on e7 moves to e5.

steps.text: To write a move down, use the piece's letter and the square it goes to: **K** king, **Q** queen, **R** rook, **B** bishop, **N** knight. Pawns have no letter, so a pawn move is just the square: **e4**. A capture adds an **x**: **Nxe5** means the knight captures on e5.

steps.title: Same board, other side
steps.prompt: Predict first: we turn the board around so you see it from Black's side. Does the name of the rook's square change?
How sure are you that you can name any square quickly, without counting? (low / medium / high)
